document.title: Explore a career at Ambi Robotics

posts.content:
In 2015, a group of University of California, Berkeley engineering students pulled broken robots from a dumpster and got to work.

Breakthroughs in Sim2Real AI, combined with good old-fashioned engineering, led Ken Goldberg and Ambi's fellow co-founders to a private demo in Palm Springs. They were told their robot was exactly what one of the world's largest ecommerce giants needed.

Ambi Robotics was born that night.

Today, fleets of robots are deployed across the U.S. and have sorted hundreds of millions of packages. Ken recently sat down with Berkeley Engineering to share the philosophy that made it possible and what comes next.

One OS capable of powering any robot for every skill doesn’t depend on one model trying to do everything. It draws from a growing library of production-proven AI skills, applying the right capability to the right robot, task, and production environment.

With AmbiOS, everything works together. It's the nervous system enabling every deployment to improve the next. 

Every AI-powered robotic system generates real-world data, retrains models, and redeploys intelligence across the fleet. This makes robotic fleets smarter, faster, and more adaptable over time.

posts.content:
Questions? Answered. 
Here’s what you need to know about CARGO:

What does CARGO do?
CARGO is an agentic Physical AI reasoning model that decides which package to stack next and where to place it, optimizing each action for a denser completed stack.

What problem does CARGO solve?
Industrial stacking is like 3D Tetris with random packages arriving continuously. CARGO plans several steps ahead because every placement changes what becomes possible next.

How does CARGO benefit customers?
CARGO builds dense stacks at production speed and adapts to new package distributions. In production evaluations, it has exceeded 72.5% density at more than 340 sorts per hour.

Does CARGO work in commercial production?
Yes. CARGO is deployed on AmbiStack systems in customer operations, achieving density comparable to manual stacking at 1.5 to 2 times the throughput.

What does CARGO unlock?
Every completed stack adds production data to AmbiOS, improving future models and expanding Physical AI reasoning to more packages, materials, and industrial tasks.

Get the details on CARGO: https://lnkd.in/eMc5tEsb
